title: Moment decomposition of the noise operator across the last coordinate
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $q$ be a nonnegative integer. Write $A$ for the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $D$ for the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, both functions on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then the $q$-th moment of $T_\rho f$ over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ decomposes as
\[
  \E_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n+1}}\!\bigl[(T_\rho f)(x)^q\bigr]
  = \E_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}\!\left[\frac{\bigl(T_\rho A(x) + \rho\,T_\rho D(x)\bigr)^{q} + \bigl(T_\rho A(x) - \rho\,T_\rho D(x)\bigr)^{q}}{2}\right],
\]
where on the right-hand side the noise operator acts on functions of $n$ variables.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n+1 variables
replaced:
For $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, writing $g = T_\rho(\mathrm{avgLast}\,f)$ and
$h = T_\rho(\mathrm{diffLast}\,f)$, the $q$-th moment of $T_\rho f$ decomposes as
\[
  \E[(T_\rho f)^q]
  = \E\!\left[\frac{(g + \rho h)^q + (g - \rho h)^q}{2}\right].
\]
